name: Yuxin Xie
heading: Compute-in-memory acceleration for machine learning
bio: I study how non-idealities in **analog compute-in-memory (CIM)** hardware affect neural network inference, and design **hardware-aware algorithms** to improve robustness and efficiency.
I am a master’s student at the School of Integrated Circuit Science and Engineering, Beihang University. I received my B.Eng. in Electronic Information Engineering from Beihang University.
interests: Efficient LLM inference and CIM acceleration

research.title: Energy-Linear Interpolation with Stability Analysis
research.summary: Analog CIM errors vary across layers and inputs. I conceived and designed a calibration method that uses the input L2 norm to condition layer-wise and column-wise compensation, combining endpoint interpolation with stratified calibration sampling.
research.result: Mean MAE decreased from 2.4350 to 2.0680 across 60 layers, using 100 frames per layer at noise level 7.0.
research.competition: Competition: Advanced Computing Technology Innovation Competition (ACTIC)

research.title: Layered training under compound noise
research.summary: Analog noise and ADC quantization pose different challenges for hardware-aware training. I conceived and designed a training framework combining Pathwise gradients for continuous noise, Hard-STE for quantization, and knowledge distillation, with an experimental design comparing gradient estimators and noise sampling strategies.
research.result: Across 12 CIFAR-10 configurations and three training seeds each, logits KD improved accuracy by about 1.02–1.34 percentage points across six gradient/sampling settings.
research.competition: Competition: 2026 Inno CIM University Challenge (存算一体高校挑战赛)
